title: Samaje Perine's 427-Yard Game: The FBS Single-Game Rushing Record
question: What is Oklahoma's single-game rushing record?
answer: Samaje Perine ran for 427 yards against Kansas on Nov. 22, 2014, as a true freshman, setting both the Oklahoma and FBS single-game rushing records. Through the 2025 season, no FBS player has topped it.
summary: Samaje Perine ran for 427 yards vs. Kansas on Nov. 22, 2014, as a true freshman, the OU and FBS single-game rushing record that still stands today.
body: Oklahoma's single-game rushing record is also the national record. On Nov. 22, 2014, true freshman Samaje Perine carried 34 times for 427 yards in a 44-7 win over Kansas in Norman, averaging 12.6 yards per carry.

The timing made it even wilder. Just one week earlier, Wisconsin's Melvin Gordon had run for 408 yards against Nebraska, breaking LaDainian Tomlinson's mark of 406 set for TCU in 1999. Perine's record took Gordon's crown after only seven days.
Perine scored five touchdowns that day, on runs of 49, 33, 34, 66 and 27 yards, and left the game once the record was his. He finished that freshman season with 1,713 rushing yards and 21 touchdowns.

Inside the OU record book, the gap between Perine and everyone else is enormous. The next-best Sooners game belongs to Greg Pruitt, with 294 yards against Kansas State in 1971, followed by De'Mond Parker's 291 against Texas in 1997 and Billy Sims's 282 against Missouri in 1979. Perine's day beat Pruitt's by 133 yards.

One of the closest calls since came from Buffalo's Jaret Patterson, who ran for 409 yards against Kent State in November 2020 before being pulled late in the game, 18 yards short. Through the 2025 season, 427 remains the FBS standard and one of the most durable records an Oklahoma player owns.
